newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait offers $38.6 mln shares in shipbuilding firm.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait offers $38.6 mln shares in shipbuilding firm.

text.p: Kuwait plans to sell 65 million shares in Kuwait Shipbuilding and Repairyard Co (KSRC) in a public offering for a total of 11.7 million dinars ($38.6 million), officials said on Saturday.
The offering, the second stage of a plan to shed most of the state's stake in KSRC, ends April 8, they said.
Kuwait sold 40 million KSRC shares in a public auction earlier this year at 206 and 208 fils, an official said. There are 1,000 fils to the dinar.
Shares will now be sold at 180 fils. KSRC shares closed at 208 fils on Wednesday.
National Bank of Kuwait (NBK), the Gulf Arab state's largest commercial bank is the underwriter and manager of the sale.
Kuwait Investment Authority (KIA), the state investment arm and the state-owned Kuwait Oil Tanker Company (KOTC) held a combined stake of 108 million of KSRC's 135.1 million subscribed shares.
KSRC's net profit rose to 5.7 million dinars in 1996 from 840,000 dinars in the previous year, according to Kuwait Stock Exchange figures.
Since the start of a wide-ranging privatisation plan in 1994, KIA has sold stakes worth over $2.0 billion in the first phase of the plan which also involves shares worth some $3.0 billion.
The second stage, involving public utilities such as electricity, water and telecommunications, is yet to start.
Only nationals of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries -- Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Bahrain -- can trade shares of Kuwaiti firms.
